title: Where do the eights fall in three different ranges?
description: Looking at the eights between one hundred and twenty and one hundred and forty, and in two higher ranges, shows the same last three digits each time. Keeko's doubt about the last two digits is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: thousands are whole eights, so the last three digits decide whether eight divides a number. Watch for students who test the last two digits only, as they did for four.

source: Find numbers between 120 and 140 that are divisible by 8. Also find numbers between 1120 and 1140, and 3120 and 3140, that are divisible by 8. What do you observe?
video_script.why: The child finds the eights in three ranges, sees that they end in the same three digits, and links this to a thousand being a whole number of eights.
video_script.substitution: Find the eights in each range by multiplying, then compare their last three digits.
video_script.anchor: three range cards laid in rows: 120 to 140, 1120 to 1140 and 3120 to 3140
video_script.wrong_answer: one thousand one hundred and twenty eight is not divisible by eight
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says one thousand one hundred and twenty eight is not divisible by eight, because its last two digits, twenty eight, are not a multiple of eight. Twenty eight is three eights with four left over, the hundreds digit adds another four, and together they make one more eight, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: The last three digits decide whether eight divides a number

final_answer.value: A number is divisible by 8 when the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8
final_answer.spoken: a number is divisible by eight when the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by eight

hold_back: Answer: A number is divisible by 8 when the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8
maths_rules: the last three digits in every range are 128 and 136
1000 = 125 x 8 and 3000 = 375 x 8, so thousands are whole eights
so a number is divisible by 8 when its last three digits make a number divisible by 8
28 = 3 x 8 + 4 and 100 = 12 x 8 + 4; the two 4s left over make one more 8, so 128 = 16 x 8
video_script.design: One idea: thousands are whole eights, so only the last three digits decide. Assumes counting in eights and the earlier test for four. Wrong idea: the last two digits decide. The three ranges stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: Answer: A number is divisible by 8 when the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The last three digits decide whether eight divides a number.
If the number they form is a multiple of eight, so is the whole number.
<bookmark mark='every'/>That is why the same endings repeat in every range.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one thousand one hundred and twenty eight is not divisible by eight.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The reason is that its last two digits, twenty eight, are not a multiple of eight.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>But twenty eight is three eights, with four left over.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>The hundreds digit adds another four, and the two fours make one more eight.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>We must read all three of the last digits together.
